source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from second PG548
source_snapshot.procedure: Logs into BMC, reads mux0x75 on i2c-tools bus5, writes0x04 to enable mux port2, and refers to PID1114953 for other expected devices.
source_snapshot.criteria: Contains only generic result/photo collection and unexpected-log language; no expected mux readback, downstream address/reply, timeout or restoration state is defined.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; incorrectly turns the supplied BMC functional I2C transaction into a physical probing/soldering test that the source never requests.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; preserves that unsupported physical-test interpretation, although it correctly flags the raw mux write as state-changing.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from second PG548
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cget -f -y 5 0x75 #Read MUX ports enabled i2ctransfer -y 5 w1@0x75 0x04 #Enable MUX Port2""
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: NO | -- not runnable by agent: testing the physical I2C connection/link between the named components (BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from second PG548) is a hardware-integrity check that requires probing/soldering the actual I2C traces and collecting photos per the criteria; the agent cannot touch the hardware or take photos over SSH.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from second PG548 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify the second PG548 path from BMC I2C-6 through mux0x75 port2 to UPHY1 using the source-specified BMC read/select and PID1114953-defined downstream replies, without mistaking a mux ACK for end-to-end connectivity.
required_package: PID1114953 second-PG548 mux0x75 port2 to UPHY1/downstream topology and expected address/reply matrix
Proof BMC logical I2C-6 maps to Linux/i2c-tools bus5
Mux0x75 register definition, port2 select value0x04, combined-bit policy and expected readbacks
Current mux owner/driver and exclusive-access window for force/raw I2C
Exact downstream transaction, reply values and bounded NACK/timeout/error criteria
Original mux byte, exact restore action, independent BMC recovery and post-restore checks
test_case.test_command: Prove BMC I2C-6 maps to i2c-tools bus5 and the second-PG548 mux0x75; record the mux byte; confirm port2 select semantics; perform the approved0x04 selection; query the exact PID-defined UPHY1/downstream endpoints; compare replies with the oracle; restore the recorded byte and verify both PG548 paths and management health.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Confirm physical probing/photos are not required unless separately approved.
safety_gate: Use only the authoritative second-PG548 bus/address map with independent management recovery available
Confirm no driver, daemon or other test owns bus5/mux0x75 before force/raw access
Capture the original byte; do not assume writing0x04 may discard other required channel bits
Allow one bounded approved select/read sequence and abort on NACK, arbitration loss, timeout, stuck bus or BMC degradation
Restore the exact recorded state and verify first/second PG548 isolation plus BMC service health
expected_evidence: PID1114953 excerpt mapping BMC I2C-6 to bus5, second PG548, mux0x75 port2 and UPHY1 endpoints
BMC identity, i2c-tools version, owner/concurrency status and health baseline
Original mux byte, approved select transcript and0x04 readback interpretation
Expected-versus-observed PID-defined downstream reply matrix with exit codes and timestamps
Bus/kernel/daemon logs and evidence that first-PG548/other channels were not disturbed
Exact restoration/readback, endpoint and service health, and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy assigns this to BMC/platform-management scope and requires controller, bus, mux, downstream address/reply and OOB/recovery mapping before execution.

source_conflict.reason: Criteria lacks an expected functional reply, while Procedure names BMC I2C-6 but commands use bus5 without mapping. DeepSeek/GPT V2 require physical probing/soldering/photos as core acceptance although the row specifies a BMC reply test, not continuity probing.
